properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): add_artifact writes `status: realized` on a file that does not exist because Artifact.status carries a schema default of `realized` that the store materialises on write, AddArtifactReq declares no `status`, and set_artifact_intent covers granularity/volatility/audience but not status — an affirmative default the defaults-do-not-assert sweep never measured, on the one type where "done" is the claim
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on the xrt-demo field report, 2026-09-16.

① OBSERVED (the agent's words): "All eight artifacts I registered — six of which do not exist yet — were written as status: realized. Nothing warned me." Expected: an artifact registered before it exists reads planned, or carries no status. NOT affected: add_capability honours an explicit status; add_decision lands proposed.

② PRECEDENT: dec:idea-four-sibling-constructors-four-status-contracts (2026-09-02) — four constructors, four status contracts; its own "NOT ESTABLISHED" line asks whether a caller can assert `realized` with nothing built. This instance is worse: no caller asserted anything; the schema did. req:defaults-do-not-assert (2026-07-28) measured ten node properties and did not include Artifact.status.

③ CANDIDATES from the design: (a) the schema default `realized` on Artifact.status, materialised on write; (b) AddArtifactReq has no `status` parameter (a reach hole, req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface's class); (c) set_artifact_intent's scope (granularity, volatility, audience) omits status; (d) the observation is wrong — the artifacts were realized in some sense.

④ ⑤ MEASURED: schema/build.yaml line 20: `status: { type: enum, values: [planned, in_progress, realized, verified], default: realized }`. AddArtifactReq (service.rs) declares id, name, artifact_type, location, description, checksum — 0 occurrences of `status`. set_artifact_intent (artifact.rs:823) sets granularity/volatility/audience. (d) refuted: beamline.json, verify.py and three images did not exist on disk. All three candidates hold together; none alone explains it — with (a) alone a caller could still correct it, with (b) alone the default would be neutral.

⑥ CLASS: an affirmative default on a status field, unreachable from the typed constructor. Same class as the 2026-09-14 checksum-acceptance default (every reconcile pass entered the fix population wearing test_failure_fix) and as Artifact.granularity/volatility/audience, which were DELIBERATELY UNDEFAULTED on 2026-08-15 for exactly this reason (music_graph F23) — the same type's neighbouring fields already carry the fix and `status` was left out. Would fixing it have stopped the earlier reports? The four-constructors report asked for the constructor to accept status (option A); this instance is the case where the not-asserting default is clearly `planned` or absent, so it does not collide with the epoch counter-example.

⑦ PIN: a test that registers an artifact with no status and asserts the stored status is not `realized` — to be written first and observed failing when the fix is built. ⑧ FIX AT THE CAUSE (not built here; his word): remove the default (absent means nobody said, like audience) or default `planned`; add `status` to add_artifact and to set_artifact_intent; migration is not retroactive, and every existing artifact keeps what it has. ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many artifacts across the field designs read `realized` for want of a choice — measurable per export.
